cmad.notes: No CMAD located. SOHO is operating (the SOHO site showed Mission Day 11261 on 2026-09-30, and ESA stated in December 2025 that SOHO still returns data daily), and NASA funds its mission operations at Goddard and the US-led instruments, so a CMAD is expected. Searched: (a) Zenodo (no SOHO CMAD; only EPHIN/ERNE calibration datasets); (b) SOHO archive pages: the sohowww.nascom.nasa.gov data and documentation pages, and umbra.nascom.nasa.gov/soho/, which holds Senior Review material for 2003–2013 but no CMAD or PDMP; (c) two rounds of web search. SOHO does not appear among the missions reviewed in the 2020 or 2023 Heliophysics Senior Review reports (checked directly). The 2023 report says missions funded as HSO Infrastructure get programmatic review instead of the Senior Review. Whether a CMAD is required under that process was not established. Treat this as a gap for the curator to check with the SOHO project scientists rather than as proof that no CMAD exists.

instrument_coverage.notes: The payload roster is the SOHO Instruments page (twelve instruments), confirmed by the SOHO About page ('The twelve instruments on board SOHO'), the twelve-instrument 'SOHO PIs' roster on the People page, the twelve instrument papers in the Solar Physics vol. 162 SOHO reference volume, and the record Description ('Twelve instruments comprised the payload'). The reverse lookup of ObservatoryID in the SMWG clone (upstream hpde/SMWG @ b8c8b803) found 13 Instrument records, all under Instrument/SOHO/ with ObservatoryID confirmed: all 12 payload instruments plus SOHO/Ephemeris, a Platform record for spacecraft positions rather than a payload instrument. Nothing is missing from SPASE. Sub-sensors such as COSTEP/EPHIN and CELIAS/SEM are not registered separately, which is expected. One minor discrepancy: the LASCO site's 'About LASCO' page calls LASCO 'one of 11 instruments' on SOHO, against twelve everywhere else.

Mission overview paper selection is confident: (Domingo et al. 1995, 10.1007/BF00733425), 'The SOHO mission: An overview', Solar Physics 162, published December 1995, the launch month. It has 'overview' in the title, names SOHO, has 1443 Crossref citations, and the record Description cites the same volume. Crossref and Semantic Scholar agree on its three authors (Semantic Scholar indexes it under the book-chapter DOI 10.1007/978-94-009-0191-9_1). With three authors there are no fourth or fifth overview authors to consider.

Instrument paper selection is confident for all twelve instruments: each is the instrument chapter of the Solar Physics vol. 162 SOHO issue (December 1995). Every title names the instrument, author counts are 13–40, and each paper matches the instrument's SPASE record or NSSDC references. Crossref and Semantic Scholar agree on authors and order for all twelve. The CELIAS, COSTEP and ERNE SPASE records link these same DOIs. Semantic Scholar merges the LASCO DOI with a 1992 conference paper by the same lead team; Crossref's 15-author list for the Solar Physics paper was used. SciX/ADS could not be queried (no API token available in this environment), so literature-index confirmation rests on Crossref plus Semantic Scholar.
Author-order detection (backward scan from the last author, followed by a check for alphabetical runs of five or more names inside each list):
- Fully not alphabetized: SUMER, SWAN, CELIAS, UVCS, VIRGO. Positions 1–3 taken.

- ERNE: partially alphabetized. The sorted suffix covers authors 10–15, and the prefix of nine contains a second sorted run at 5–9. Positions 1–3 (Torsti, Valtonen, Lumme) are outside both runs and taken.
- GOLF: partially alphabetized. The sorted suffix covers authors 7–31 (Bocchia … van der Raay, with 'van der Raay' filed under V), so the prefix is 6. Prefix positions 1–3 taken.

- MDI: partially alphabetized. The sorted suffix covers authors 7–12 (Rosenberg–Zayer), but prefix authors 2–6 (Bogart, Bush, Hoeksema, Kosovichev, Schou) are also in alphabetical order. The list reads as Scherrer followed by two alphabetized groups, so only Scherrer is taken. Bogart and Bush are excluded, erring against position evidence as the ambiguity rule requires.

- EIT, CDS, COSTEP, LASCO: the backward scan finds no sorted suffix, but each list contains an alphabetized institutional block reaching into the top three: EIT 2–7 (Artzner–Song), CDS 3–12 (Carter–Pike), COSTEP 3–8 (Fleißner–Sierks), LASCO 1–7 (Brueckner–Socker). A run of five or more sorted names is the skill's own threshold for deliberate alphabetization, so authors inside these blocks got no position evidence: Artzner, Brunaud, Carter, Fleißner, Koomen, and Howard's LASCO position.

- LASCO's block starts at author 1. Brueckner's lead position was kept because ESA independently names him LASCO PI (ESA information note 11-1996). The same group-lead-first pattern appears elsewhere in the list (Lamy for LAS, Schwenn for MPAe, Simnett for Birmingham).
- Short sorted runs below the five-name threshold were treated as chance and positions were used: VIRGO 1–4 (Fröhlich, Romero, Roth, Wehrli), GOLF prefix 3–6, SWAN 1–3, UVCS 2–4.
- The MDI author list ends with 'The MDI Engineering Team', a team name that generates no candidate.

Observatory-run scoping: from each instrument, only the leads are taken. That means description-paper positions 1–3, excluding those inside alphabetized blocks; every qualifying-role Contact in the Instrument record; the PI named in the NSSDC Master Catalog entry the Instrument record links; and the current PI named on the SOHO mission's People page. Positions 4 and 5 of every instrument paper are recorded as excluded instrument-team depth.

Instrument-paper authors at position 6 or later (about 250 people across the twelve papers) are not listed individually, because position gives them no evidence. Tail authors who have independent evidence do have entries: Fludra, Boumier, Strachan, Gurman, Poland, Domingo, Howard, Hoeksema, Hochedez, Michels, Gabriel, Marsch, Torsti and Culhane.

Evidence weighting for provider pages: on an Observatory record the Strong 'PI named on the provider's official pages' tier is reserved for a mission PI. SOHO has no mission PI; the mission-level leads are the ESA and NASA project scientists. Instrument PIs named on the SOHO People page or in ESA and NASA notes were therefore weighted Medium, as provider team-page evidence.

SOHO People page (https://sohowww.nascom.nasa.gov/about/people.html, last modified 2026-07-23): only the displayed entries were used. The HTML source also contains about two dozen commented-out, undisplayed roster entries from earlier years; these were not used as evidence. The commented-out 'SOHO PIs' entries for Klecker (CELIAS), Bertaux (SWAN), Torsti and Valtonen (ERNE) are recorded as Low context on those people's entries only.

SPASE Contacts are stale for 9 of 12 instruments. The 2019 records (CDS, EIT, GOLF, LASCO, MDI, SUMER, SWAN, UVCS, VIRGO) list the founding-era PI from NSSDC, while the SOHO People page names a different current PI for all of these except MDI (Scherrer). The 2023 records (CELIAS, COSTEP, ERNE) list the current PIs. No Instrument record carries FormerPI, CoPI or CoInvestigator roles. Curators may want to add the current PIs and mark the founding PIs as FormerPI.

NSSDC Master Catalog: every live URL (spacecraft and experiment pages, including those in the SPASE records) returned an error page on 2026-09-30, so archived Wayback copies from 2024–2025 were used for the experiment pages. The MDI entry (ex=12 / -12) had no usable archive copy, and the spacecraft-level page was not retrieved. The SPASE InformationURLs pointing to NSSDC may need checking later.

REVIEWER FLAG — J. Leonard Culhane: the SOHO/UVCS SPASE record and the NSSDC UVCS entry both list him as a UVCS Principal Investigator alongside Kohl, and he is included at Medium on that basis. Nothing else corroborates it: he is not among the 40 UVCS paper authors, the SOHO PI roster names Strachan, and the pre-flight UVCS description is by Kohl & Noci (Kohl & Noci 1992, ESA SP-348). He does appear as the 15th author of the CDS paper, misspelled 'J. L. Gulhane' in Crossref. This may be an error carried from NSSDC into SPASE. Confirm before publishing an InstrumentLead role.

REVIEWER FLAG — founding-era PI roles recorded as InstrumentLead: Harrison, Hovestadt, Kunow, Delaboudinière, Torsti, Gabriel, Brueckner, Howard, Wilhelm, Bertaux, Kohl and Fröhlich are recorded as InstrumentLead because their sources say 'Principal Investigator'. Each role_evidence names the current PI on the SOHO roster, so the role agent can decide whether FormerPI is more appropriate.

REVIEWER FLAG — mission project scientists: ESA's SOHO Project Scientist is Daniel Müller (since 2023), and NASA's is Jack Ireland (December 2025). Bernhard Fleck's ProjectScientist role comes from the SPASE Observatory Contacts and may be historical. Joseph B. Gurman's comes from the 2013 Senior Review proposal. Neither Vicente Domingo nor Arthur I. Poland was given a ProjectScientist role, because no fetched source states one, even though they were widely known as the launch-era ESA and NASA project scientists. A curator may add it with a source.

REVIEWER FLAG — CELIAS PI succession: NSSDC names Hovestadt, and the SOHO roster names Wimmer-Schweingruber. A commented-out roster entry suggests Klecker held the CELIAS PI role in between; the CELIAS Instrument-record run should confirm this.

Anik De Groof and George Dimitoglou co-authored the 2025 Nature Astronomy mission retrospective (Müller et al. 2025, 10.1038/s41550-025-02687-4), but no fetched source states a SOHO role for either, so both are excluded. A reviewer who knows their mission roles (for example ESA or NASA SOHO operations) may add evidence.
The ESA and NASA 30th-anniversary articles also quote agency officials who are not SOHO team members. They were not treated as candidates.

Links not added to information_urls: the CDS home page (solar.bnsc.rl.ac.uk) did not respond; the SWAN Service d'Aéronomie page returns 404, and the FMI SWAN link lands on a generic FMI page; the European SOHO site (soho.esac.esa.int) did not respond; and the HelioData mission page is JavaScript-only, so its content could not be read. On 2026-10-01 the relabel under the clarified 'Out-of-date Contacts' rule was applied using evidence already gathered, with no new searches. For all 12 instruments the live 'SOHO PIs' roster on the SOHO People page names a sitting PI. Every other included person whose PI listing comes only from SPASE Contacts, the NSSDC catalog or the 1996 ESA note is therefore recorded as FormerPI of that instrument, with the successor named. Thirteen people changed: Harrison, Hovestadt, Kunow, Delaboudinière, Torsti, Gabriel, Brueckner, Howard, Wilhelm, Bertaux, Kohl, Culhane and Fröhlich. Scherrer stays InstrumentLead for MDI because the roster names him as current PI. Each instrument now has exactly one InstrumentLead. This supersedes the earlier reviewer flag about founding-era PIs recorded as InstrumentLead. Culhane is kept included as FormerPI of UVCS, and his role_evidence notes the possible NSSDC error.
